Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are out in the middle and the players of Sri Lanka Women form a huddle and sprint onto the field. It will be the left-hand/right-hand combination of Alyssa Healy and Beth Mooney to open the innings for Australia Women. Udeshika Prabodani, the left-arm pacer to get proceedings underway with the ball. Let's play...
... The Run Chase ...

Right then, just 94 runs needed for Australia Women to start their quest for a seventh title with a win. The pitch is a bit difficult to start on but in all honesty, this shouldn't be a tough chase by any means. Sri Lanka Women will have to come hard at the Aussies and will need some quick wickets in the Powerplay if they are to make a match of this one. Join us in a bit for the run chase.

Sri Lanka Women came into the tournament with a lot of promise but they have now put on a couple of under-par performances with the bat and their talismanic skipper, Chamari Athapaththu hasn't been able to get a hit with the bat either. They lost wickets front up as both openers flopped and all the pressure then fell onto the shoulders of Harshitha Madhavi who tried to anchor the innings but got out on 23. It was then Nilakshika Silva who managed to muster up some hard-fought runs and remained unbeaten on 29 off 40 balls that got them over the 90-run mark.

It was not quite a vintage performance from Australia Women in the field but one that was good enough to keep Sri Lanka Women down under the 100-run mark. Megan Schutt started things up well for the Aussies, bowling tight lines and picking up a wicket as well. However, she bowled a couple of no balls and then Darcie Brown came in and bowled three more no balls. The spinners though, kept things tight and got wickets at regular intervals, not allowing the Lankans to find those crucial boundaries. Schutt then came back in to finish off the innings and picked up a couple of more wickets which took her T20 World Cup tally to 43, equalling Shabnim Ismail's record for the most wickets in the history of the tournament.

Another one on the shorter side. The pull shot comes out again. This is hit through square leg. One run again. That's a fine last over and that's the end of a Lankan innings that has struggled throughout! They finish with just 93/7 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, big swing across the line from Harshitha Samarawickrama and she almost gets cleaned up here. Megan Schutt pitches the ball up on off and middle, getting it to just angle in a bit, Samarawickrama swings across the line but the ball goes inches over the stumps.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Megan Schutt to Harshitha Samarawickrama, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Changes the angle of attack by coming around the stumps and darts the ball back into middle, Samarawickrama stays leg side of the ball and pushes it out on the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Megan Schutt to Harshitha Samarawickrama, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pitches it up around leg and gets it to angle across towards off and middle, Harshitha Samarawickrama plays it on the up and towards covers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Megan Schutt to Harshitha Samarawickrama, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Floated, full and around off, driven away past the diving fielder at covers for a single by Samarawickrama.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Ash Gardner to Harshitha Samarawickrama, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Madhavi is taken completely aback there. Ash Gardner tosses it up and ends up serving a juicy full toss, Harshitha Samarawickrama ends up in an awkward position and just about manages to keep it out on the leg side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Ash Gardner to Harshitha Samarawickrama, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slows it up and flights it onto middle and leg, Harshitha Samarawickrama watches it well and defends it out with soft hands.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Ash Gardner to Harshitha Samarawickrama, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Dropped short on the pads, Kaveesha Dilhari turns it off the hips and wide of backward square leg for a single. Off the mark right away.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Ash Gardner to Kaveesha Dilhari, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Kaveesha Dilhari is the next batter in.

OUT! LBW! Another huge appeal for LBW but this time it is turned down by the umpire. Ash Gardner goes straight to her captain and Alyssa Healy opts for the review. This is a tossed-up delivery, drifted onto middle and leg, Chamari Athapaththu goes down for the sweep and misses, getting hit on the pads. Nothing on UltraEdge and the main question is whether the ball went with the arm or spun away. Ball Tracking shows that the ball hit the back pad and it would have hit the leg stump. The original decision is overturned and both Lankan openers are now back in the hut.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Ash Gardner to Chamari Athapaththu, OUT! lbw b Ash Gardner.

Commentary.Commentary: Tossed up around off, hint of turn away from the left-hander, Athapaththu watches it well and blocks it to the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Ash Gardner to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Harshitha Samarawickrama is in at number 3.

OUT! LBW! A huge appeal for LBW and the finger is raised. Vishmi Gunarathne reviews it pretty quickly though and the third umpire is called into action. Megan Schutt bowls this one on a good length and outside off, darting it back in towards the stumps, Vishmi just looks to get inside the line and flick it away but is caught on the crease and is pinged on the pads. The replays roll in and no bat involved. Ball Tracking comes up with three reds and young Vishmi has to walk back for a duck. Sri Lanka Women 6/1 after 3 overs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Megan Schutt to Vishmi Gunarathne, OUT! lbw b Megan Schutt.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowled full and straight at the stumps, Vishmi Gunarathne drives it on the up but straight to mid on.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Megan Schutt to Vishmi Gunarathne, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nice change-up from Megan! Slower one, floated up full and wide, this one goes away from the right-hander. Another no ball called as Megan has overstepped once again, cardinal sin. Vishmi Gunarathne will have another chance at the Free Hit.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Megan Schutt to Vishmi Gunarathne, No ball!

Commentary.Commentary: No ball! This is fuller and around off, Athapaththu drives it away through the cover region for a single. There is a late call for no ball as Megan Schutt has overstepped and a Free Hit will now follow...
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Megan Schutt to Chamari Athapaththu, No ball!

Commentary.Commentary: First runs off the bat! Good length, angling away from the left-hander, Athapaththu reaches out and drives it behind point for a couple of runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Megan Schutt to Chamari Athapaththu, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Nagging length around leg and finishing on the middle stump line, Athapaththu hops back to defend it with a straight bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Megan Schutt to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: A tad full and angled well across the off stump, Athapaththu looks to drive and misses and Alyssa Healy spills another one.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Megan Schutt to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hard length on leg, angling away towards the off pole, Athapaththu stays put and just past it back onto the deck. Watchful start from the Lankan openers.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Megan Schutt to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Lovely delivery to end the over and Ash Gardner too begins with a maiden. Flighted ball on the fifth stump line, getting it to dip, Vishmi Gunarathne is drawn forward but the ball zips past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Ash Gardner to Vishmi Gunarathne, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Sri Lanka Women are finally off the mark but it will be a leg bye. Too full and angled into the pads, Athapaththu looks to whip it away but misses and the ball clips the pads, rolling past short fine.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Ash Gardner to Chamari Athapaththu, Leg bye.

Commentary.Commentary: Shortens the length on off, Athapaththu gets on the back foot and punches it away to point.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Ash Gardner to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nicely tossed up, on middle and Athapaththu blocks it off the front foot.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Ash Gardner to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Flighted ball on the pads, just angling down, Athapaththu looks to tickle it fine but gets it off the pads and the keeper spills it down.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Ash Gardner to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Around the wicket to the left-hander, drifted into the pads and this one slides right on and hits the pads of Chamari Athapaththu.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Ash Gardner to Chamari Athapaththu, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Spin from the other end as Ash Gardner has been tossed the ball.
A maiden to begin with from Megan Schutt, top stuff! Fullish length on off, shaping back in a fair bit, Gunarathne looks to drive but misses and wears it on the pads yet again.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Megan Schutt to Vishmi Gunarathne, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Good length, in line with the stumps, Gunarathne solidly blocks it off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Megan Schutt to Vishmi Gunarathne, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Alyssa Healy is now standing up to the stumps. Megan Schutt pitches it up around off, Gunarathne looks to push at it but gets an outside edge that goes down towards short third.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Megan Schutt to Vishmi Gunarathne, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Just a touch fuller, on a good length and swinging back into the batter, Gunarathne is tentative to get forward and gets beaten on the inside edge, taking a blow on the pads.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Megan Schutt to Vishmi Gunarathne, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Bowled back of a length again and around off, this one straightens a touch, Vishmi Gunarathne looks to block off the back foot but misses and gets hit on the body.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Megan Schutt to Vishmi Gunarathne, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Begins from over the wicket, and straightaway goes wide on the crease as well. This is dropped short outside off, angling it in a long way. Vishmi Gunarathne covers the line and blocks it off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Megan Schutt to Vishmi Gunarathne, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Done and dusted with the pre-match proceedings and it is now time to get the play underway. The players of Australia Women can be seen in a huddle, all smiles as well with skipper Alyssa Healy handing some final words of wisdom. The umpires walk out to the middle and so does the opening pair for Sri Lanka Women - Chamari Athapaththu and Vishmi Gunarathne. The Australians take their places on the field and it will be the veteran pacer Megan Schutt to take the new ball. Let's play...

Just a few minutes left for this match to get underway but first up, the players along with their mascots will line up for their respective national anthems. It will be the national anthem of Sri Lanka first, followed by the national anthem of Australia.

PITCH REPORT - Natalie Germanos and Lisa Sthalekar are pitchside. Natalie starts by saying that it is pretty hot at 36 degrees Celsius but there is a good breeze blowing. Adds that the dimensions are lob-sided and it is pitch number 3 that is being used for this game. Lisa adds that the key factor in the previous two games was that the bowlers were bowling on a good length and slower too. However, this pitch doesn't have the same grass cover as the previous one and it should skid more than spin.

Australia Women skipper, Alyssa Healy says she doesn’t mind bowling first. Adds there’s calmness around the group and they feel they are well prepared and it’s just about adapting. Gives a little information about her team and confirms that Phoebe Litchfield is back from her injury.

Chamari Athapaththu, the captain of Sri Lanka Women says she’s very confident about her batting lineup and hence, wants to bat first. Mentions they have to execute their plans well and play some positive cricket. Informs that they have made one change with Inoka Ranaweera coming in for Sachini Nisansala.

Sri Lanka Women (Playing XI) - Vishmi Gunarathne, Chamari Athapaththu (C), Harshitha Madhavi, Kaveesha Dilhari, Nilakshika Silva, Hasini Perera, Anushka Sanjeewani (WK), Sugandika Kumari, Inoshi Fernando, Inoka Ranaweera (In for Sachini Nisansala), Udeshika Prabodani.

Australia Women (Playing XI) - Alyssa Healy (C/WK), Beth Mooney, Ellyse Perry, Ash Gardner, Phoebe Litchfield, Tahlia McGrath, Georgia Wareham, Annabel Sutherland, Sophie Molineux, Megan Schutt, Darcie Brown.
TOSS - Sri Lanka Women have won the toss and they will BAT first.

The first two games in Sharjah saw low-scoring encounters, both won by the team batting first and given the afternoon heat and pitch conditions, we might see teams opting to bat first here as well. Will Sri Lanka Women be able to push the Aussies to their limits? Or will Australia Women start off their quest for another title with a win? Only time will tell. Toss and team news in a bit, stay tuned.

Sri Lanka Women on the other hand did come into the tournament as one of the dark horses but suffered an unexpected defeat against Pakistan Women in their opening encounter and now have their task cut out against the mighty Aussies as well. Skipper Chamari Athapaththu will be key as the Lankans look to pull off an upset but it won't be an easy task as they have never beaten Australia Women in a T20I.

The women from 'Down Under' always walk into a big tournament as one of the favorites to win it all and this time won't be any different, especially given the fact that they have won the last three editions of the tournament. They've had good success heading into the World Cup with a series win against the White Ferns, followed by a couple of straightforward victories in the warm-up matches and will be raring to get their campaign underway on the right foot.

Hello and a very warm welcome to one and all! The 2024 edition of the ICC Women's World Cup has kicked off in fine fashion and it is yet another doubleheader day. Reigning champions, Australia Women are all set to get their campaign underway against the reigning Asian Champions, Sri Lanka Women in Sharjah in what will be a Group A clash.
... MATCH DAY ...

As the grand spectacle of the ICC Women’s T20 World Cup unfolds, attention shifts to Match 5, where the Australian Women’s team launch their campaign against the Sri Lankan Women, who are set to take the field at the Sharjah Cricket Stadium after having already played a game. The defending champions, Australia Women, are clear favourites for this match, but the determination of the Sri Lankan team could present a formidable challenge. Australia made the most of their warm-up games, clinching convincing victories in both. The firepower at the top of their lineup, featuring stars like Alyssa Healy, Beth Mooney and Ellyse Perry positions this team as a dominant force. Their middle order is equally impressive, bolstered by a strong group of all-rounders, including Ash Gardner, Tahlia McGrath and Annabel Sutherland, all of whom are expected to play pivotal roles in the tournament. With spin-friendly pitches in play, it will be intriguing to see who joins Megan Schutt in anchoring the pace bowling unit. On the other hand, Sri Lanka Women faced a setback against Pakistan Women in their opening clash, despite being in a commanding position at the halfway mark. After bowling Pakistan out for just 116 runs, thanks to impressive performances from Udeshika Prabodani, Sugandika Kumari and skipper Chamari Athapaththu, their batting order faltered dramatically. Only two players managed to reach double figures, leaving them with a meagre total of 85 runs for the loss of 9 wickets, resulting in a disappointing 31-run defeat. That defeat adds immense pressure on the Sri Lankan team to put their best foot forward and deliver a significant challenge to Australia. They will need to regroup and show resilience if they hope to make an impact. With Australia Women eager to kick off their campaign with a victory and Sri Lanka Women determined to turn the tables and secure crucial points, this match promises to be an exciting affair. The stage is set for a thrilling contest, and it will be fascinating to see who comes out on top. Who are you backing for the win? Time will soon tell!
